results.title: When the subgroup of squares has odd order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite commutative group, $G^2=\{x^2:x\in G\}$ its subgroup of squares and $G[2]=\{x\in G:x^2=1\}$ its 2-torsion. Then $|G^2|$ is odd if and only if $G[2]\cap G^2=1$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.summary: For $n\ge1$ the *genus map* of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ is the homomorphism indexed by the primes $q\mid n$. Let $n>1$ be odd and squarefree and $t=|T_n|$. Then the image of the genus map has at least $2^{t-1}$ elements.

results.title: The principal genus theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n>1$ be odd and squarefree, $\mathrm{Cl}$ the class group of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $t=|T_n|$. Then the subgroup of squares is the intersection of the kernels of the genus characters, which is the kernel of the genus map, and $|\mathrm{Cl}[2]|=2^{t-1}$.

results.title: The 2-rank of the class group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n>1$ be odd and squarefree, $\mathrm{Cl}$ the class group of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $t=|T_n|$. Then $|\mathrm{Cl}[2]|=2^{t-1}$, and the kernel of the ambiguous class map $\psi:\mathbb F_2^{T_n}\to\mathrm{Cl}$ has exactly two elements.

results.title: The 4-rank statement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The *4-rank statement* is the following assertion. For every odd squarefree $n>1$, the genus class number $g(n)$ is odd if and only if every $e\in\mathbb F_2^{T_n}$ with is $0$ or $e_n$. Here $R$ is the Rédei matrix of $n$, and $e_n\in\mathbb F_2^{T_n}$ is $1$ at the primes of $n$ and $0$ at $2$; it is the exponent vector of the ideal $(\sqrt{-n})$.

results.title: Rédei's theorem on the 4-rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The 4-rank statement holds: for every odd squarefree $n>1$, the genus class number $g(n)=|\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n}))^2|$ is odd if and only if every vector $e\in\mathbb F_2^{T_n}$ killed by the Rédei matrix of $n$ is $0$ or $e_n$. Here $e_n$ is $1$ at the primes of $n$ and $0$ at $2$, and it is nonzero for $n>1$.
